core_investment_rationale: Pass 3 research conclusion: WATCHLIST, MEDIUM confidence. Local demand/supply density, Mobility cash generation and growing Delivery contribution can compound SBC-inclusive operating earnings and cash per share. At the dated $71.62 price, base value $59-85 (centre about $70) offered no clear margin of safety; this is research classification, not a portfolio decision.
key_assumptions: Analyst base scenario: five-year bookings CAGR about 14%; EBIT/bookings rises from 3.11% to 4.5%, economic operating FCFF from $5.67B to $12.91B. Not company guidance.

Valuation-sensitive: base WACC 10.5%, terminal growth 3%, terminal cash tax 23%, incremental ROIC 25%; about 74% of base value is terminal. Fixed diluted denominator 2.050225B; no free buyback uplift.
Reverse DCF at the dated price requires about 18.8% economic FCF CAGR to $13.42B in year five; model inference, not observed market consensus.
TTM reported FCF $10.116B differs from normalized cash FCF $7.22-7.62B and shareholder economic FCF $5.28-5.68B. Insurance, tax, leases and SBC matter; proxies are not audited measures.
AV remains MIXED: hybrid demand aggregation may preserve value; direct customer channels and fleet guarantees may compress contribution or raise capital intensity.
Standalone operating forecast plus existing holdings; Delivery Hero future closing is not already consolidated. Incremental deal NPV=0 is a modelling convention, not evidence of no risk.

Already known at baseline: Delivery Hero offer and existing stake/TRS exposure; announced Rivian/Lucid AV commitments; final prospectus for EUR4.5B bonds with expected September 15 settlement, not yet completed on September 14. Repetition is not a new change; actual settlement, new terms or financial consequences may be.
growth_drivers: Organic Mobility demand and local matching density.
Delivery, advertising and cross-platform monetization with operating leverage; incremental merchant economics must remain sustainable.
SBC-inclusive operating profit and sustainable cash per share growth; gross bookings alone are insufficient.
moat_or_competitive_assumptions: Mobility has a real but conditional local density advantage; group-wide monopoly or wide moat is not established.
Low switching costs, multihoming and city-level competitors limit pricing power.
AV distribution value depends on customer relationship, partner utilization and net contribution after capital commitments.
key_risks: Insurance/claims and regulatory or labor costs impair unit economics.
Reported FCF overstates sustainable owner economics if reserve timing, cash tax and recurring SBC are ignored.
AV direct channels weaken demand ownership and contribution; fleet funding or guarantees raise capital burden.
M&A, Delivery Hero financing and private holdings realization may reduce financial flexibility or earn below the cost of capital.
Valuation requires strong growth and margin execution; lower growth and flat margins do not support the dated price.
invalidation_conditions: Loss of repeat demand relationship or structural take-rate/contribution compression.
Insurance or regulation causes negative unit economics.
Large acquisition/fleet commitments earn below cost of capital for a prolonged period.
Monitoring warnings: worsening same-city retention/wait times despite higher promotions; lower merchant contribution after advertising; direct AV channels achieve comparable utilization without Uber.
key_kpis: Organic gross bookings, trips, frequency and acquisition-adjusted segment contribution.
GAAP EBIT/bookings and SBC-inclusive Mobility/Delivery segment operating income/bookings.
Reported-to-normalized FCF bridge, insurance claims/recoverables, cash taxes, leases and SBC.
Diluted economic cash/share and actual share count; capital committed to M&A and AV.

Research reassessment triggers: economic cash >=$6.5B and cash/share >=$3.15 with flat/down share count, not reserve/tax timing; bookings growth around >15% and EBIT/GB >=3.6% for two reporting periods. These are not automatic promotion rules.
catalysts: New reporting periods clarify cash conversion and margin durability.
Delivery Hero closing, financing and retained-asset economics become clearer.
AV agreements disclose net contribution and binding Uber capital obligations.
Dated research valuation reassessment bands: $50-55 if business assumptions hold; $55-60 only with stronger cash/margin evidence. Not entry orders.
open_questions: Insurance claims/recoverables net cash bridge and sustainable float benefit remain unresolved.
September cash, debt and share denominator update; private holdings realizable value.
Recurring SBC replacement cost and sustainable shareholder cash conversion.
AV vehicle financing, residual value and minimum utilization/revenue guarantees: who bears binding risk and what return remains?
Delivery Hero post-closing net economics, financing and capital return.
Incremental cross-platform/merchant returns and city/cohort retention are incompletely disclosed.
